title: Hop-aware carrier probe for bounded cross-process tracing and lossy transport resilience
creator: Nina Park
description:
Goal: add a lightweight, backwards-compatible "hop-aware" carrier header and SDK middleware that keeps cross-process tracing headers bounded in size, survives lossy transports (websockets, SQS-like queues, HTTP proxies that drop long headers), and preserves enough provenance to stitch traces while avoiding header bloat.

Motivation: We've seen production incidents where large baggage + multi-hop routing resulted in headers > 8KB causing proxies to drop headers or RPCs to truncate context, which breaks sampling attribution and increases false-negative traces in latency/error dashboards. Existing approaches either accept unbounded baggage or move everything to sidecars; neither is acceptable for lightweight SDKs used on mobile/edge.

Scope: implement carrier format v1 and middleware for Node/Python/Go SDKs, runtime request-proxy shim to recompute hop-count and compact baggage, and an optional server-side replayable small-store (ttl-indexed) to recover truncated context for high-value requests. The PRD and design doc outline upgrade path and rollout constraints.

Design highlights and choices made: 
- Carrier header: TRACE-CARRIER-V1 (base64-url-safe payload). Payload contains: trace_id (16b hex), span_id (8b hex), sampling_hint (enum), hop_count (u8), compacted_kv (prefix-filtered k=v pairs up to 512 bytes), checksum (4 bytes).
- Hop-count semantics: each process increments hop_count. Receivers may prune compacted_kv when hop_count > threshold (configurable, default 4). Pruning strategy is deterministic: keep keys with highest retention priority (trace_id, origin, service.short, span.kind, short_error_tag).
- Lossy transport resilience: when header missing or truncated, middleware will attempt context lookup against a short-lived in-memory LRU store keyed by (trace_id,last_seen_ts) if the request carries a short reference token produced by SDKs when they previously exported a context (optional feature gated by config).
- Backwards compatibility: old SDKs ignore unknown header names. New SDKs fall back to standard W3C Traceparent if present. We avoid changing existing trace IDs or sampling decisions.
- Size guardrails: compacted_kv max 512 bytes; final header capped at ~1KB. If compaction alone cannot reduce size, SDK will drop the least important keys and set sampling_hint=unknown.

Trade-offs considered: 
- We could offload full baggage to a sidecar or store for all requests but that increases operational footprint and RT cost. We prefer small header + optional short-store for high-value traffic to balance reliability and cost.
- Deterministic pruning is slightly more complex but avoids nondeterministic downstream differences during trace stitching.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: intermediate proxies still drop headers under some load shapes. Mitigation: ensure SDKs emit short reference token in body/query for high-value requests and instrument console dashboards to surface header-drop rate per region.
- Risk: wrong pruning removes important diagnostic tags. Mitigation: expose SDK config for retention priorities and a safe-mode that preserves error/signature tags.

Design docs and artifacts (links): see design doc and rollout checklist.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Nina Park: Kickoff meeting notes: aligned on header format, retention priority list, and store-as-fallback approach. Action: produce design doc and example middleware for node sdk.
2026-03-03 - Mateo Rojas: POC implemented for Node. Verified header stays <1KB for common baggage sets. Found edge-case with AWS ALB stripping headers >8192 — added short-reference token fallback.
2026-03-06 - Design review (Priya): Suggest exposing retention priority as named presets (debug, default, compact). Agreed and added to config plan.
2026-03-08 - Security review (Samir): raised question about reference token placement in body/query. We decided to make it opt-in and signed with HMAC using KMS key id to avoid replay risk.

2026-03-10 - Mateo: Integrated fallback LRU store prototype behind feature flag telemetry.hop_carrier_lookup. Benchmarks (local): negligible latency impact for hits, ~0.6ms median for miss path when store cold.
2026-03-12 - PR feedback (ENG telemetry team): request unit tests around pruning determinism and interop tests with legacy clients. Added TODOs in PR.

2026-03-14 - QA (Elena): test matrix drafted for transport variants (http1/2, websocket, grpc, sqs). Found truncation behavior on edge proxy staging; updated staging proxy config to allow TRACE-CARRIER-V1 and short token headers through.
2026-03-14 - Mateo: Rolling out canary to telemetry-staging with node sdk v2.18 - feature flag on. Monitoring header-presence, dropped headers, and trace stitching success rate.
acceptance_criteria: SDK middleware written for Node, Python, Go and published behind feature flag
Header format validated with interop tests against legacy W3C traceparent flows
Canary rollout shows <0.1% increase in request latency median and 80% reduction in header-drop trace gaps in staging
Deterministic pruning unit tests and fuzz tests added (CI coverage)
Runbook updated with steps to toggle short-store and inspect header-drop dashboards
testing_plan: Integration tests across http1/http2/grpc/websocket bridges. Interop tests with older SDKs. Chaos tests simulate header truncation and verify fallback short-store repair path. Load tests to ensure LRU store scales under production QPS with feature flag off/on.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal SDKs in staging behind feature flag (2 weeks). Phase 2: canary in production for low-traffic services and telemetry ingest (1 week). Phase 3: opt-in for customer-facing SDKs, provide migration guide (4 weeks). Final: flag on by default and release docs (TBD).
notes: Follow-up items: instrumentation to track how often pruning drops each key, create a Console alert for sustained header-drop >0.05% per region, and coordinate with infra to ensure edge proxies are configured to allow TRACE-CARRIER-V1 and short-token headers.
